# Priority Processor

[alpha]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#alpha

The Priority Processor is a memory-pressure-aware admission controller
for trace spans, designed for the **bridges**-style telemetry pipeline.
It mirrors the OTel `memory_limiter` processor's configuration and
behavior at the threshold edges, with one priority-aware divergence
between the soft and hard marks: spans carrying the `_br` breadcrumb
attribute (checkpoint / "bridge breadcrumb" spans emitted by the SB SDK
processor — its presence on the wire IS the priority signal, matching
the simulator's emit-iff-checkpoint model) are kept by **evicting
non-checkpoint spans from an internal LIFO buffer**, until no more
non-checkpoint spans are available to sacrifice.

## Behavior

Each `check_interval` tick samples container memory (cgroup v2
`memory.current`, falling back to v1 `memory.usage_in_bytes`, then to
`runtime.MemStats.Sys`) and classifies the processor into one of three
zones:

| Zone | Condition | Incoming checkpoint span (carries `_br`) | Incoming non-checkpoint span |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NoPressure** | `alloc < soft` | admit → hp buffer | admit → lp buffer |
| **SoftPressure**, lp buffer non-empty | `soft ≤ alloc < hard` | admit → hp buffer; evict 1 lp span (LIFO) | drop |
| **SoftPressure**, lp buffer empty | `soft ≤ alloc < hard` | drop | drop |
| **HardPressure** | `alloc ≥ hard` | drop | drop |

Where `soft = limit - spike` (derived from the two configured
percentages).

At the **lp-empty under soft** and **hard** zones, behavior is
**identical to `memory_limiter`** — both refuse all spans. The only
divergence is the "grace zone" where the processor sacrifices
non-checkpoint spans to keep absorbing checkpoint spans. Once that
grace runs out (no more lp to evict, or memory crosses the hard mark),
the processor falls back to the same all-refuse behavior the standard
`memory_limiter` would have at the same memory level.

Buffered spans are forwarded to the next consumer in the pipeline by a
periodic flush goroutine (every 100 ms by default), regrouped into
proper `ResourceSpans` / `ScopeSpans` structure.

## Configuration

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `limit_percentage` | uint32 | `80` | Hard ceiling, as a percentage of container memory. Above this, all spans are refused (matches `memory_limiter.limit_percentage`). |
| `spike_limit_percentage` | uint32 | `20` | Burst headroom above the soft mark, as a percentage of container memory. Soft mark = `limit - spike`. Matches `memory_limiter.spike_limit_percentage`. |
| `check_interval` | duration | `1s` | How often the memory probe runs. Matches `memory_limiter.check_interval`. |

Validation: `spike_limit_percentage < limit_percentage` (otherwise the
soft mark would be ≤ 0 and the grace zone would vanish).

### Example pipeline

```yaml
processors:
  priority:
    limit_percentage:       80
    spike_limit_percentage: 20
    check_interval:         1s
  batch:

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers:  [otlp]
      processors: [priority, batch]
      exporters:  [otlp]
```

The processor is intended to **replace** `memory_limiter` in a pipeline
that uses the SB SDK processor upstream (which writes `_br` only on
checkpoint spans, matching the simulator's wire format). It is NOT
additive — running `priority` and `memory_limiter` together would
double-shed under pressure.

## Metrics

The processor emits one structured log line per second under the name
`priority_processor_metrics`. Fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | Current zone (`none` / `soft` / `hard`) |
| `alloc_bytes` / `soft_limit_bytes` / `hard_limit_bytes` | Sampled memory and thresholds |
| `hp_buf_depth` / `lp_buf_depth` | Current internal buffer depth, per priority |
| `cp_admitted` / `lp_admitted` | Cumulative admit counts, per priority |
| `cp_dropped` / `lp_dropped` | Cumulative drop counts, per priority |
| `lp_evicted` | Cumulative non-checkpoint evictions performed to make room for incoming checkpoints |
| `flush_spans_sent` / `flush_batches_sent` | Spans/batches successfully handed off to the next consumer |
| `flush_spans_failed` / `flush_batches_failed` | Spans/batches whose downstream consume returned an error |

Tail via:

```bash
kubectl logs ds/<otelcol-daemonset> | grep priority_processor_metrics
```

## Notes

- `_br` is set on each checkpoint span by the SB SDK processor based on
  the span's structural position in the trace (depth%cpd==0, or any
  leaf-server kind). The attribute is stripped from non-checkpoint
  spans before export, so its presence on the wire is the priority
  signal — no separate flag, no value to parse. The priority processor
  itself does not classify spans, it only routes them.
- LIFO eviction (newest non-checkpoint span first) is intentional: a
  burst of incoming spans is the typical pressure pattern, and we'd
  rather keep older non-checkpoint context than the freshly-arrived
  burst that's driving the spike.
- Internal buffers are bounded by overall process memory (the check
  loop catches them), NOT by a separate explicit buffer-bytes cap.
  This matches `memory_limiter`'s approach exactly.
